items.title: Lew Tabackin interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 17, 1999
items.q: Toshiko has the advantage. She writes all the music, she conducts, and she does everything. I play a lot of solos... We play a steady Monday night at Birdland here in New York

ctx.x: Yeah? I was going to ask before.

You know, we don’t have to be so pretentious. Flute player would do. Band leader? Not really. That’s kind of like — Toshiko has the advantage. She writes all the music, she conducts, and she does everything. I play a lot of solos and occasionally call people up and do a little contracting work. But I’m a pretty bad band leader. In fact sometimes she has to take off. We play a steady Monday night at Birdland here in New York, and occasionally she might be in Japan and she’ll say well do that. So I do it, and it’s…
Okay. Well at least you’re honest.
